dedupe_keys.name: carb 2021 agricultural equipment emission inventory california

description: This inventory estimates the population, activity, fuel use and emissions of self-propelled off-road diesel equipment used in California agriculture, updating CARB's 2011 inventory. It draws on an anonymous statewide survey of 2018 farm sizes, crops and equipment use, grouped by role such as producer, custom operator, first processor and rental company, together with the USDA 2017 Census of Agriculture, 2018 county agricultural commissioners' data and EIA agricultural diesel use, with crops in twelve commodity types, equipment in fifteen categories and horsepower bins. It was produced by the California Air Resources Board in August 2021. Coverage is California, with the San Joaquin Valley, which holds 56% of harvested acres, treated separately. The technical documentation is free to download as a PDF; no licence is stated. Findings include a fall in the valley's estimated 2018 equipment population from 83,600 to 68,500, over 7,000 more Tier 4 final tractors than projected by 2024, fuel use 19% above the 2011 estimate and a projected 0.9% yearly decline in equipment. Caveats: survey results are anonymised and extrapolated. For simulation it gives equipment counts, activity and fuel demand of farm machinery, useful for agricultural energy demand, fuel supply disruption and electrification scenarios. It is related to the AEM tractor and combine sales reports record in this catalogue.
